labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE, SANDBOXED: PERQemu 0.9.5 (C# on Mono, SDL2; github.com/skeezicsb/PERQemu, GPLv3) emulates a Three Rivers PERQ-1A (16K CPU, 2 MB, CIO+OIO, 768x1024 portrait display, Kriz tablet, 14-inch Shugart) running POS G.7 — inside a systemd-nspawn container with private PID/mount/net/user/ipc/uts namespaces (host uid range 2359296+, read-only debootstrap trixie rootfs, only work/ and the X socket dir writable, capabilities dropped, @mount filtered; the operator's host-application rule after the medley incident). Xvfb :98 at 768x1048 lives INSIDE the container; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11). No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel, no network. LOGIN: user `guest`, empty password, at the `Please enter your name:` prompt (press Return first to accept the default date). KEYS: XTEST, proven drop-free at 80 ms/char. POINTER: PASS — XTEST absolute, the Kriz tablet is absolute and PERQemu maps the host pointer 1:1 onto it; two-target readback in docs/lab/PERQ-WAVE.md §Pointer. PERQemu NEEDS A TTY: its CLI GetLine() is the emulator's clock, so perq-inner.sh runs mono under script(1) with an explicit stty size; without it the machine never ticks (docs/lab/PERQ-WAVE.md §Walls). Reset=relaunch: fresh copy of Disks/g7.prqm + cold boot, shell in ~45 s; PERQemu 0.9.5 has no save state. Drive it with xdotool on DISPLAY=:98 from labrun, or `labctl shot perq`.

pointer.device: host X pointer over XTEST (root coordinates are Kriz-tablet pixels; PERQemu maps the host pointer 1:1 onto the Kriz tablet, absolute, no offset/scale) + POS keyboard over XTEST keys. Two-target readback (2026-09-13): commanded root (200,300) -> sprite origin (200,299); commanded root (600,800) -> sprite origin (600,799). 1:1 identity, measured with a 2 s settle after each XTEST warp (an immediate screendump missed the move; PERQemu's console-clocked poll loop needs a tick to pick up the new position).

museum.blurb: The first commercial workstation with a bitmapped display and a pointing device — Pittsburgh, 1980, a year before the Xerox Star. Its 16-bit CPU has no fixed instruction set: writable microcode makes it a Pascal machine, and so is POS.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station, HOST-NATIVE and CONTAINED: PERQemu 0.9.5 (J. Dersch and S. Boondoggle, GPLv3) runs on Mono inside a systemd-nspawn sandbox with an Xvfb of its own; the daemon captures the X root and drives XTEST. The PERQ's portrait screen is 768x1024 and the root is 768x1048 — PERQemu shrinks its window below any root exactly 1024 lines tall, so the extra 24 lines buy a full-size, non-panning display. Reset = relaunch from a pristine copy of the POS G.7 disk; PERQemu 0.9.5 has no save state, and a cold boot to the shell takes about 45 s. See docs/guests/perq.md and docs/lab/PERQ-WAVE.md.

emulator.version: 0.9.5 (upstream release zip, run on Debian trixie mono-runtime-sgen inside the station's container)
emulator.driver: PERQ-1A, CIO + OIO, portrait display, Kriz tablet, 14-inch Shugart (PERQemu `configure` script in perq-inner.sh)

network.note: No network: the OIO board's Ethernet is configured in PERQemu but has no host side, and the container has --private-network (lo only). POS G.7 has no TCP/IP stack. No retronet reservation is held.

reset.mouse: PASS (2026-09-13) — XTEST absolute (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test) against the PERQ's absolute Kriz tablet, two-target readback by the perq-ptr stream: commanded root (200,300) -> sprite origin (200,299); commanded root (600,800) -> sprite origin (600,799). 1:1 identity, no offset/scale, measured with a 2 s settle after each XTEST warp (PERQemu's console-clocked poll loop needs a tick to pick up the new pointer position). POS draws its own arrow cursor sprite directly on the character console, no graphical tool needed. See docs/lab/PERQ-WAVE.md §Pointer.
reset.keyboard: PASS (2026-09-13) — XTEST keys reach POS through the PERQemu SDL window on :98, drop-free at 80 ms/char: Return accepted the boot date prompt, `guest` typed 4/4 characters at the `Please enter your name:` prompt and an empty password logged in to the POS shell. Frames 02-after-return / 04-shell / 06-guest / 07-shell in docs/lab/PERQ-WAVE.md.
reset.fixture: POS G.7 at its shell prompt: the a-boot banner and disk partition table (boot/accent/paging/user), the login transcript, the `sys:User>Guest>` status line with the running clock, and the `>` prompt. resetMode=relaunch with no state: the launcher copies Disks/g7.prqm fresh into the container's work/ and cold-boots PERQemu; the login prompt is up ~20 s after power-on and the shell ~45 s. PERQemu 0.9.5 has NO save state, so there is no checkpoint to recapture — the pristine disk plus the boot script IS the golden.
